chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Isa ibn Bashir, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When death approached Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), he pressed me to his chest, then said: 'O my son! I bequeath to you what my father (peace be upon him) bequeathed to me when death approached him, and what he mentioned that his father bequeathed to him.'
He said: 'O my son! Beware of the injustice of one who cannot find a helper against you except for Allah.'

key_terms.أُوصِيكَ: I bequeath to you / I advise you

ai.seo_question: What is the key ethical instruction regarding oppression mentioned in the final bequest of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the continuous chain of moral bequests (waṣiyyah) within the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically linking Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn to his father, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn, and ultimately to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib. It emphasizes the concept of 'zulm al-gharib' (oppression of the stranger/weak) as a critical spiritual danger, warning that the oppressor bears the burden of judgment before Allah when no human advocate remains. This narration serves as a foundational text in Shia ethics for maintaining justice even over those who cannot retaliate, reflecting the Imams' role as guardians of divine justice.
